title: Change an Apple Watch band: hold the release button while the old half slides out, then slide the new half in
instruction: Change the band's top half for the new one: hold the band release button for the top slot while you slide the old half out, then slide the new half in, printed side up, until it clicks.
context: Apple Watch owners change bands often, and Apple's own page teaches how: 'Hold down the band release button, then slide the band across to remove it' and 'slide the new band in until you feel and hear a click'. The button sits on the back beside the slot and retracts the catch only while it is held, so one fingertip holds it, on a button 8 mm long, while the other hand draws the band's bar out along its slot. Pulled without the button, the catch holds the bar. The new half's bar must then meet the slot square and level and go in straight to the catch, with the watch kept still. A picture cannot answer it: the hard part is the held press during the draw and the millimetre fit. Here a watch lies face down on a pad with a black band fitted, and a new white half lies beside it. Apple and Apple Watch are trademarks of Apple Inc., named for identification only.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. (1) Pad: 25 x 24 cm, 3 mm thick, centred (34, -8), rigid, friction 0.6 (estimates). (2) Watch: Apple Watch Series 11 46 mm aluminium case, 46 x 39 x 9.7 mm (Apple tech specs), 52 g with the fitted hole half (the watch alone is listed at 37.8 g), face down, centred (33.8, 0), crown end toward +x, friction on the pad 0.5. (3) Band slot across the crown end, along y: a channel 5.6 mm wide (x) and 5.0 mm tall (z), open at the -y side and closed by a stop 12.5 mm from its middle, with a slit 3.2 mm tall on its +x side for the strap. The bar is 24 mm long, 3.6 mm deep and 3.0 mm tall, so it has 1.0 mm a side in the slot (the real clearance is about 0.2 mm, an estimate; widened for the simulator). (4) Band release button on the back above the slot at (35.5, 0): 8 x 3.5 mm, standing 0.5 mm proud, in 0.5 mm at 3.75 N, spring 7,500 N/m (estimates from maker photos; the real button is nearer flush). (5) Catch: a sprung pawl 3 x 2 mm that drops into a 3 mm notch in the bar's top when the bar is within 0.5 mm of centred and the button is up, and lifts out while the button is in more than 0.3 mm. It holds the bar against any pull the arm gives; the catch force is not published. (6) Sport Band, 46 mm: each half is a bar, a neck through the slit and a rigid strap 24 mm wide, 3 mm thick; pin half 90 mm, 12 g (estimates; the real strap is soft, the bar is rigid). The old (black) pin half is fitted at the crown-end slot, its strap lying on the pad toward +x. The old hole half is fixed to the watch's other end. The new (white) pin half lies flat on the pad, printed side up, its bar's centre at (36, -15), its strap toward +x. Frictions: strap on pad 0.6, bar in slot 0.6 (estimates). Both arms start at their ready pose with grippers open. Reset: old half in its slot, new half on its mark.
scoring: Judged when both grippers are 3 cm clear and all has been still for 1 s. Old half out of the slot: 0.25. Plus new half in, centred within 0.5 mm, catch in its notch, button up, printed side up, watch within 3 cm of its start and level: 1.0. Check: it won't slide out without the button.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz), about 2.8 times the 43 s demo
fidelity: Rigid bodies: the strap is a rigid bar (the real one flexes), the pad is rigid. Slot clearance 1.0 mm a side (real about 0.2). Button, catch, slot and frictions are estimates; no maker figures. Code stands in for the catch's spring and cam: the pawl follows the button's joint and the bar's pose. The old hole half is fixed to the case. The demo reads object poses to steer.
scores: Scripted demo 1.0 on GPU physics, 3 of 3 runs at the final settings (866 steps, 43 s). Lazy routes: nothing 0; draw without the button 0 (the catch holds the bar); new half 6 mm short of the catch 0.25. Dream-1: 0 in 2,400 steps.
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Between real trials fit the old half and lay the new half on its mark.
